traditional_remedy: Use mature cow-dung compost or vermicompost to support soil health.
Apply diluted panchagavya only according to local guidance.
organic_remedy: No treatment is required; avoid preventive spraying without need.
Remove only damaged or senescent leaves with clean tools.

disease.description: The model identified a visual pattern consistent with {disease}. Confirm in the field before applying treatment.
symptoms: Look for expanding spots, discolouration, curling, or lesions.
Compare nearby plants and inspect both leaf surfaces.
disease.cause: May be associated with fungal, bacterial, viral, or pest pressure; a field inspection confirms the cause.
traditional_remedy: Remove heavily affected leaves and dispose of them away from the compost pile.
Use a neem-oil spray only at the label dilution and test it on a few leaves first.
Keep soil covered with clean organic mulch; do not let mulch touch stems.
organic_remedy: Improve airflow and keep foliage dry by watering at soil level.
For fungal-looking symptoms, consider an approved organic treatment after local advice.
Avoid mixing home remedies or exceeding product directions.
disease.application: Recheck after 5–7 days. Treat in cool, dry conditions and stop if foliage shows burn.
prevention: Rotate crops and remove volunteer plants.
Sanitize pruning tools and avoid handling wet foliage.
Use balanced compost rather than excess nitrogen.

Tomato___Late_blight.severity: High — can spread quickly in cool, wet weather
symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches often begin at leaf edges.
Brown lesions may expand rapidly after rain or overhead irrigation.
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete infection favoured by prolonged leaf wetness and cool, humid conditions.

Potato___Late_blight.severity: High — act promptly and seek local extension guidance
symptoms: Dark, water-soaked leaf lesions can spread rapidly.
White growth may appear under leaves in humid weather.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete infection favoured by humid, cool conditions.

symptoms: Older leaves can develop brown spots with concentric rings.
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal disease often encouraged by wet foliage and stressed plants.

symptoms: Olive-brown to black velvety leaf spots.
Spots can appear on fruit as the season progresses.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungal spores spread in wet spring conditions.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.severity: High — manage vectors and remove severely affected plants
symptoms: Upward leaf curling and yellowing of new growth.
Stunted plant growth and reduced fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Viral disease commonly transmitted by whiteflies.
